newsitem.title: USA: Johnson says Q3 drug sales up 13.7 pct.
newsitem.headline: Johnson says Q3 drug sales up 13.7 pct.

text.p: Johnson and Johnson said on Wednesday that its worldwide pharmaceutical sales rose 13.7 percent in the third quarter, fueled primarily by the strong growth of 23.1 percent in the United States.
It did not give dollar figures for the drug sales. The company reported total third quarter worldwide sales of $5.40 billion versus $4.74 billion a year ago.
It posted third quarter earnings per share of $0.56 versus $0.48. First Call consensus for the quarter was $0.55.
Worldwide sales in Johnson and Johnson's professional segment rose 19.2 percent in the quarter, with a 22.9 percent increase in the United States and 14.8 percent internationally.

Strong sales growth in the unit came from J&J's merger this year with Cordis Corp as well as further professional acceptance of the Palmaz-Schatz Coronary Stent, the company said. A stent is a small metal tube-like structure used to hold open arteries.

J&J's worldwide consumer sales increased by 8.4 percent, with U.S. and international sales up 11.6 percent and 5.2 percent respectively. It cited growth in its Tylenol line of analgesic and cold products, among other products.
